title: What can you say about collagen peptides in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for collagen peptides; the strongest is "Provides amino acids the body uses to build protein, including muscle protein" (moderate, 2.6-10 g hydrolyzed collagen a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Helps manage joint pain, or relieves joint pain".

supported_wordings.wording: Provides amino acids the body uses to build protein, including muscle protein.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it based on collagen's amino acid content; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada also accepts a smaller amount if it supplies at least set minimums of each amino acid named.

supported_wordings.wording: Provides lysine, which helps the body form collagen.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: up to 10 g hydrolyzed collagen a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: The daily amount must supply at least 133 mg lysine; the maximum is 10 g hydrolyzed collagen. Adults 18 and older.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Helps manage joint pain, or relieves joint pain
wordings_to_avoid.why: FDA's 2000 rule (page 1016) says 'joint pain' is characteristic of arthritis, so joint-pain wording is a disease claim in a US review.
Names a disease. Health Canada lists osteoarthritis wording, but it names a disease; the joint-pain wording without a disease name is listed separately.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Rebuilds cartilage in damaged or arthritic joints
wordings_to_avoid.why: Implies reversing joint disease; no listed source supports it.
Compares the product to a drug.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
